paragraphs.source_en: On the twelfth day of the second month of Keichō 8, Tokugawa Ieyasu was formally appointed Seii Taishōgun by imperial decree. By then, six months had passed since the death of Ieyasu's mother, Odai.

units.source_en: On the twelfth day of the second month of Keichō 8, Tokugawa Ieyasu was formally appointed Seii Taishōgun by imperial decree.
units.source_zh: 庆长八年二月十二，德川家康被正式敕封为征夷大将军。

units.source_en: By then, six months had passed since the death of Ieyasu's mother, Odai.
units.source_zh: 其时家康生母於大去世已半年。

paragraphs.source_zh: 庆长八年二月十二，德川家康被正式敕封为征夷大将军。其时家康生母於大去世已半年。

paragraphs.source_en: That New Year, as custom required, the daimyō first went to Osaka to offer Toyotomi Hideyori their New Year greetings, then proceeded to Fushimi Castle to pay their respects to Ieyasu. Although Ieyasu held the realm's power in his hands, everyone still regarded Hideyori as the one and only young lord.

units.source_en: That New Year, as custom required, the daimyō first went to Osaka to offer Toyotomi Hideyori their New Year greetings, then proceeded to Fushimi Castle to pay their respects to Ieyasu.
units.source_zh: 是岁新年，诸大名按例先去大坂向丰臣秀赖道贺新春，然后转往伏见城给家康拜年。

units.source_en: Although Ieyasu held the realm's power in his hands, everyone still regarded Hideyori as the one and only young lord.
units.source_zh: 家康虽手握天下权柄，但众人依然认为，秀赖乃是不二的“少君”。

paragraphs.source_zh: 是岁新年，诸大名按例先去大坂向丰臣秀赖道贺新春，然后转往伏见城给家康拜年。家康虽手握天下权柄，但众人依然认为，秀赖乃是不二的“少君”。

paragraphs.source_en: The shogun's ceremony of imperial thanksgiving was held on the twenty-fifth day of the third month.

units.source_en: The shogun's ceremony of imperial thanksgiving was held on the twenty-fifth day of the third month.
units.source_zh: 将军谢恩仪式于三月二十五举行。

paragraphs.source_zh: 将军谢恩仪式于三月二十五举行。

paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu and his retinue departed Fushimi for Nijō Castle on the twenty-first day of the third month; on the twenty-fifth, they reached the Imperial Palace at the second quarter of the Hour of the Serpent.

units.source_en: Ieyasu and his retinue departed Fushimi for Nijō Castle on the twenty-first day of the third month;
units.source_zh: 家康一行三月二十一从伏见出发前往二条城；

units.source_en: on the twenty-fifth, they reached the Imperial Palace at the second quarter of the Hour of the Serpent.
units.source_zh: 二十五日，到达皇宫，时为巳时二刻。

paragraphs.source_zh: 家康一行三月二十一从伏见出发前往二条城；二十五日，到达皇宫，时为巳时二刻。

paragraphs.source_en: As an offering of gratitude, Ieyasu presented the Emperor with one thousand ingots of silver; as New Year gifts, he also offered one hundred bolts of brocade, one hundred ingots of silver, and a celebrated sword. Nor was that all: Ieyasu sent gifts individually even to the imperial princes and titled court ladies.

units.source_en: As an offering of gratitude, Ieyasu presented the Emperor with one thousand ingots of silver; as New Year gifts, he also offered one hundred bolts of brocade, one hundred ingots of silver, and a celebrated sword.
units.source_zh: 家康向天子献上白银千锭以为谢仪，还奉上锦缎百匹、白银百锭和名刀一把，以为新年贺礼。

units.source_en: Nor was that all: Ieyasu sent gifts individually even to the imperial princes and titled court ladies.

paragraphs.source_en: By the time he withdrew from the palace, it was already the fourth quarter of the Hour of the Horse. Thus Odai's dearest wish was fulfilled: the Nitta shogun had supplanted the Ashikaga shoguns, who were likewise of Minamoto blood.

units.source_en: By the time he withdrew from the palace, it was already the fourth quarter of the Hour of the Horse.
units.source_zh: 从宫中告退，时已午时四刻。

units.source_en: Thus Odai's dearest wish was fulfilled: the Nitta shogun had supplanted the Ashikaga shoguns, who were likewise of Minamoto blood.
units.source_zh: 至此，於大心愿达成，新田将军取代了同为源氏的足利将军。

paragraphs.source_zh: 从宫中告退，时已午时四刻。至此，於大心愿达成，新田将军取代了同为源氏的足利将军。

paragraphs.source_en: When Chaya Yajirō Kiyotsugu saw the audience procession leave the Imperial Palace, he set out for the port of Sakai to visit Naya Shōan.

units.source_en: When Chaya Yajirō Kiyotsugu saw the audience procession leave the Imperial Palace, he set out for the port of Sakai to visit Naya Shōan.

paragraphs.source_zh: 茶屋又四郎清次见面圣的队伍出了皇宫，便朝堺港而去，他要去探望纳屋蕉庵。

paragraphs.source_en: Naya Shōan was old and frail, and this illness had confined him to bed with little hope of recovery; he had therefore asked Yajirō to go to the capital and witness Ieyasu's investiture with his own eyes.

paragraphs.source_zh: 纳屋蕉庵年迈体衰，此次卧床，恐难有康复之日，故他请又四郎进京亲眼一观家康的受封仪式。

paragraphs.source_en: When the regulations governing red-seal ships were established in Bunroku 1, there were only nine such vessels in the entire country.

paragraphs.source_en: Kyoto's Chaya, Suminokura, and Fushimiya had one each; Iyoya of Sakai, Suetsugu Heizō of Nagasaki, Araki Sōemon, and Itoya Zuemon each had one; and Funamoto Yaheiji had two—

units.source_en: Kyoto's Chaya, Suminokura, and Fushimiya had one each; Iyoya of Sakai, Suetsugu Heizō of Nagasaki, Araki Sōemon, and Itoya Zuemon each had one; and Funamoto Yaheiji had two—
units.source_zh: 京都茶屋、角仓、伏见屋各一艘， 堺港伊予屋、长崎末次平藏、荒木宗右卫门、丝屋随右卫门各一艘，船本弥平次两艘——

paragraphs.source_en: Eleven years later, the number of red-seal ships was no longer remotely comparable to what it had been. This was due first to Ieyasu's protection, but also to a maxim Naya Shōan never tired of repeating: if the red-seal fleet reached three hundred ships, the uprisings and disturbances within the realm would be halved.

paragraphs.source_en: In the meantime, Naya Shōan had fallen ill, and the physician had pronounced his recovery hopeless. Though he falsely claimed to have forgotten his age, a rough reckoning put him past eighty. That was why Chaya Yajirō was frantic with anxiety as he boarded the boat prepared for him and hurried toward Sakai.

paragraphs.source_en: Chaya was making this journey expressly to visit the old man; how bitterly disappointing it would be if Shōan had already lost consciousness by the time he arrived. paragraphs.source_en: “Row faster! The old man carries the whole realm in his heart. The boat sped down the Yodo River with the current.

paragraphs.source_en: It was late at night when Yajirō Kiyotsugu reached Shōan's retreat by Chigomori Shrine. As he approached Shōan's residence, Yajirō's heart remained gripped by unease. If the old man had already died, lanterns would surely be hanging high at the main gate. No obituary had reached him, but might something have changed during his journey?
